chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I went out while my wife was menstruating, and when I returned, she was pregnant.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked him, 'Whom do you accuse?' He said, 'I accuse two men.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Bring them.' So he brought them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'If this is his son, he will be born as a cat, such and such.' So he was born just as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had said. So his maternal family protected him from the people, and his inheritance is for them; and if a person had said to him, 'O son of the adulteress,' he would be whipped with the legal punishment (Hadd).

key_terms.قَطَطاً: A cat (or small animal, used here as a sign of paternity)
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ الْحَدَّ: He is whipped with the legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paternity accusation and the Hadd punishment for calling someone 'son of the adulteress' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia legal principle of 'Istishab' (presumption of continuity) and the specific mechanism of paternity determination through physical signs, where the child's birth characteristics confirm the accused father's identity. It highlights the social and legal protection afforded to the child, ensuring he is not stigmatized as illegitimate ('Ibn al-Zanī') unless explicitly accused, in which case the accuser receives the Hadd punishment. The narrative underscores the Prophet's role in resolving familial disputes through divine insight into physical lineage markers.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Dawood Bin Farqad,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to Rasool-Allahsaww, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! I went out and my wife was menstruating. So when I came back, she was pregnant’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to him: ‘Whom are you accusing?’ He said, ‘They are two men’. Hesaww said: ‘Come with both of them’. So he came with both of them. So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘If this is his son, it would come out as a cat’. So it came out just as Rasool-Allahsaww had said. So its mother’s family went out protecting it from the people, and his inheritance is for them; and had it been a human being, and it was said to him, ‘O son of an adulteress’, he (the accuser) would be whipped the legal punishment (Hadd)’.
